findings.description: The ADR-010 row's status cell is a truncated fragment: 'Accepted (partially superseded by ADR-015: the SkiaSharp library'. The parenthetical is never closed, the sentence ends mid-clause, and the cell omits the second recorded supersession (the renderer-configuration clauses superseded by ADR-019) that ADR-010's own Status line carries. The decisions index is one of the enumerated current-state surfaces for this task and the acceptance criteria require it to carry no stale or malformed claim; a reader cannot tell what ADR-010's current standing is. The defect is pre-existing (introduced by commit 13c8033, 'Split decisions, changelog, and limitations'), not introduced by 21.2, and it is not a v1.2 staleness, so it does not affect the v1.2 state this task reconciles. The worker's verification of this file cited only '29 index rows == 29 ADR files' and a 'proposed' grep; scripts/check-docs.sh likewise validates only the row count, so neither check covers cell integrity. Note the same truncation exists in ADR-010.md's own Status block, which is immutable decision text and must not be rewritten; only the index cell is in scope.
evidence: docs/decisions/00-index.md:18 '| ADR-010 | V1 Renderer Implementation Contract | Accepted (partially superseded by ADR-015: the SkiaSharp library | [`ADR-010.md`](ADR-010.md) |' - unbalanced parenthesis; the only row in the file with unbalanced parentheses (awk paren-count check over rows 9-37 flags line 18 only).

docs/decisions/ADR-010.md:3-10 carries the full status: 'Accepted (partially superseded by ADR-015: ...; the renderer-configuration clauses that keep geometry, placement, and scale code-owned are superseded by ADR-019)'. The index cell reproduces only its first clause.
git log -L 18,18:docs/decisions/00-index.md -> the row has been truncated since 13c8033, the file's creation; no later commit touched it.
scripts/check-docs.sh:46 compares only `adr_rows` to `adr_files`, so the truncation is invisible to the guard.
findings.recommended_action: Complete the ADR-010 index cell to match the full relation recorded in ADR-010.md's Status line (ADR-015 partial supersession plus the ADR-019 renderer-configuration supersession), and consider adding a check-docs guard that rejects an unbalanced parenthesis or an unterminated status cell in the decisions index so the class cannot recur. Because ADR-010.md's own Status text carries the same truncation, decide explicitly whether that is an intentional carry-over of the historical record or an independent defect to record; do not rewrite ADR decision text without that decision.

limitations: Scope was limited to the canonical current-state surfaces enumerated in the task. The v1.2 artifact identity, docs/release/build-and-release.md, manifest.json, and the release test matrix are task 21.3; the release changelog entry, the current_release block, and the v1.2.0 tag are task 21.6. README.md's manual-install section still names the v1.1 package `ArrTags_1.1.0.0.zip` and tag `v1.1.0`; that is correct for the current release and is 21.3's to update, not a defect here.

No build or test run was performed and none is required: the change set touches no code, and the worker's claim that the full suite was not run is accurate and appropriate for a documentation-only task.

The v1.2 live pinned-host matrix is task 21.4 and has not run, so no current-state claim in the reconciled surfaces asserts v1.2 live verification. Spot-checking was limited to confirming that cited evidence paths exist and that the specific claims they support are present in the shipped code (config.html, LogSubject.cs, ByteLimitUnits.cs, RestartRequiredSettings.cs, the Diagnostics sources, the reconciliation cursor and discard-reason sources, and the named test files).

ADR text was treated as immutable decision record throughout. Where an ADR and current behaviour diverge, the divergence was recorded as a finding rather than reconciled by editing the ADR; this applies to ADR-010's truncated Status block (F-21.2-D1) and to the F4/F6/F7/F8 'open.md' references in ADR-022/023/024/026/029, which point at entries that now live in archive.md. Those ADR-internal pointers are not surfaced by any current-state claim and ADR-025 already records the register move in its implementation note, so they were judged not to be a current-state defect; the general pattern (a resolved limitation leaving a stale 'docs/limitations/open.md' pointer inside ADR References sections) is worth a future sweep.

This reviewer did not evaluate whether the reconciled wording is the wording a product owner would choose; it evaluated only whether each current-state claim is supported by the repository and the recorded evidence.
summary: The v1.2 current state is described accurately across the enumerated surfaces, and the task's specific acceptance criteria are met. F3, F4, F6, F7, and F8 are recorded Resolved in the register, the index, and state.json, each with its resolving phase, its evidence list, and explicit verification bounds and registered residuals; open.md is empty of them. F5 is Accepted (reclassified from Open) in accepted.md, the index, and state.json, with the exclusion recorded in docs/planning/v1.2.md section 10 and matching README's shipped-limitation framing. ADR-022 through ADR-029 are all Accepted (v1.2) and every amendment/supersession relation (ADR-024 into ADR-002/003/009, ADR-026 into ADR-020, ADR-027 into ADR-019, ADR-028 into ADR-016, ADR-029 into ADR-022 clause 3) is recorded on both the newer ADR and the older index row, with no ADR decision text rewritten. No surface presents v1.2-fixed behaviour as missing or open, and README claims no capability the code does not ship: the diagnostics panel, ExtraLarge, the MB/KB limit presentation with exact-byte persistence, the restart-required note text plus best-effort modal, and the bounded file-name log subject were each confirmed in the shipped configuration page, the cited source files, and the registered limitations. The register's 52 section headings match its 52 index rows exactly in both ID and title. The worker's edits stayed inside the delegated current-state surfaces, touched no immutable history, and left the generated blocks current (render-docs-state --check: up to date; PLANS.md and state.json agree), and its F1 correction is supported by task 14.3's PASS matrix including its Goal C inventory-cache row. Six findings are recorded, none of which makes a v1.2 claim wrong or overclaimed: one MEDIUM pre-existing defect the worker's evidence did not cover (the truncated ADR-010 status cell in the decisions index, which the row-count guard cannot see), one LOW pre-existing v1.1-vintage residue in two dated data-model notes that read as pending work, and four informational items (the SEC-2 title/status tension, the expected agent-pairing transient, an incomplete residual enumeration inside V11-G4, and the ADR-022..ADR-028 versus 'ADR-022 onward' bound difference between the planner-owned status surfaces and GOALS.md). The last of these is a genuine cross-surface consistency gap but every statement in it is true, and the owning role is the planner, so recording rather than resolving it was correct. Status is PASS_WITH_FINDINGS: the reconciliation itself is complete and evidence-backed, and the open items are narrow, pre-existing, and none blocks the v1.2 release.
